_comment: Run from packages/gateway-whatsapp (pnpm --filter @theokit/gateway-whatsapp run test:mutation); deliberately NOT wired into `test`, so `pnpm -r run test` in CI never pays for it. The pattern is copied from packages/gateway, which was the only package in this repo ever measured this way. mutate is scoped to the five files that are pure logic and nothing else: allowlist.ts decides WHO MAY TALK TO THE BOT, inbound-rules.ts applies it and the group rule to every inbound path (in scope since 2026-10-06), split.ts decides where a long message breaks, errors.ts maps platform failures onto typed codes, backend/cloud/signature.ts decides whether a webhook POST is Meta's (in scope since 2026-10-06; the normalizers left in webhook.ts are not measured yet). inbound-rules.ts also holds the foreign phone number id check. adapter.ts is excluded because it is I/O orchestration whose tests drive a fake backend, and the bridge is a .mjs child process Stryker cannot instrument. break=95 is the MEASURED baseline (95.86% on 2026-08-30; 95.38% on 2026-10-06 over 238 mutants with inbound-rules.ts in scope; 96.90% over 290 mutants with signature.ts added the same day) with headroom for two mutants. The first run of this config scored 73.96%; the difference is 37 mutants killed by tests written against them, not by scope changes -- that pass did not move the mutate list. Every remaining survivor is enumerated with its reason in tests/MUTATION.md, and anything not on that list is outstanding work. Raise this when the score rises; never lower it to make a red run green under an unchanged scope. The cross-package map — every baseline, what is excluded from scope and why, and the two shapes of survivor that recur — is in docs/MUTATION.md.
